_note: Every change that moves a published number or its meaning, newest first. methodology.json publishes these entries and methodology_version = the newest date. Add an entry in the same commit as the change.

entries.change: /changes now diffs every page's lead numbers against the previous publish, not only the CPI readings: the compute indexes, each power hub's 30-day average, the 10-year, BBB yield, high-yield spread and 30-day SOFR, copper, the capacity tracker, the long-lead package prices and the DC and gauge headlines. Movers rank by their change divided by a stated notable move for that reading (for example 3% for a power hub, 5bp for the 10-year), a design threshold rather than a fitted volatility, and the page leads with the day's biggest AI-infrastructure move.

/rates adds what the AI builders paid on their latest USD notes: each issuer's most recent deal, read from its own filing (SEC pricing term sheets for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle; CoreWeave's pricing release; Nebius's 6-K). These are new-issue terms on the pricing date, not live yields. A spread the term sheet states is shown as stated; CoreWeave's is computed as its coupon (priced at par) minus the Treasury curve that day at the note's maturity. Convertible notes are listed but not compared. Microsoft has issued no USD bonds since 2017 and is left out.

The long-lead board drops industrial pumps (no vendor states a usable figure) and now covers four packages, 45% of DC Build. Gas turbines and fuel cells join the generator row: GE Vernova's Power segment and Siemens Energy Gas Services as their own vendor entries, with GE's turbine backlog stated in gigawatts and its contracted slots into 2031 as a lead time, and Bloom Energy's fuel-cell backlog, which Bloom states only with its full-year results. In DC Build the pumps line keeps its 5% weight and its series (BLS pumps & compressors PPI); it is relabelled 'Pumps & compressors (cooling-loop proxy)', since no price index covers coolant distribution units or chilled-water loops. Nothing is restated. /commodities now publishes each wholesale power hub's 30-day average, its YoY and its 30-day change (the window /power uses) instead of the latest single day's print, which swings several-fold.

The token price index moves to the most-used models on OpenRouter by paid spend (its rankings, week to Oct 7; free, stealth and preview models excluded): Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Grok 4.7, Qwen3.8 Max, Mistral Large 4 and Llama 4 Maverick leave. Nothing is restated: the index keeps its July base, the departing models link up to their last collected price, and the changeover day links flat if fewer than three models are priced on both days. Each model now carries a frontier, standard or light tier label, after Ramp's split of enterprise model spend; the label never weights the index. The roster is reviewed monthly against the same rankings.

The token price index moves to a current model roster: GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Grok 4.7, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen3.8 Max, Mistral Large 4 and Llama 4 Maverick, replacing GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 5, Llama 3.1 70B, DeepSeek Chat, Gemini 3.5 Flash and the 2024 Mistral Large. Nothing is restated: the index keeps its July base. The old models link up to their last collected price and drop out the next day, and the new models join the links as they are priced, so the roster change alters which price moves are averaged, not the level. A link with fewer than three models priced on both days (for example, a changeover with no common day) is flat. /compute also adds on-demand list prices per GPU-hour from AWS, Azure, Oracle Cloud and CoreWeave. All A100 rows are the 80GB part. A quote older than its staleness limit shows its date and drops out of the price ranges and the cheapest-price mark. These prices sit beside the vast.ai marketplace medians and never enter the GPU index.

The DC Hardware storage component rides NAND spot prices again past the last storage-device PPI, under a stricter rule. NAND history now reaches back to 2019 through Wayback Machine snapshots of the same DRAMeXchange page, and the PPI's own release history (ALFRED) makes the backtest grade what readers actually saw. The tail rides only while NAND is more than 50% away from its level a year earlier; in calmer markets carrying the last print forward wins, because half of this PPI's first prints since 2020 repeat the prior month. Its worst graded month must be no worse than carry-forward's, replacing a fixed 10-point bound no rule could meet in the 2026 memory shock (carry-forward itself missed July 2026 by 58.6 YoY points). The 50% threshold and the relative bound were both set after seeing the 2020-26 backtest. Over 75 graded months the switched tail at pass-through 0.1 averaged 2.81 YoY points of error against 2.99 for carry-forward. Hardware YoY 29.3% (storage official, Aug +87.2%) to 32.1% (storage tail +105.7% through Oct 1).

For EIA residential electricity and gas, which now extend BLS only past the last print on a like-month ratio, the one-day quality hold tests the change against the same months a year earlier instead of the raw step. The raw step includes BLS's own seasonal move from a year ago, which the old level splice showed can exceed 5% (EIA residential gas moves more than 5% in about half of all months). In practice EIA publishes after BLS, so neither component has had a tail since 2026-09-26 and the gate has not run on them. The change prevents a seasonal turn from being held when a tail does appear.

Used cars no longer count the Manheim wholesale move twice in the 12-month outlook and the CPI nowcast. The trend was read off Manheim-spliced levels and the Manheim forward driver was then added on top. With the driver live, the trend now comes from the official CPI used-car series. Store 2026-09-28: the outlook's used-car path went from -0.69 to -0.55%/mo in months 1-3 and from -0.20 to -0.06%/mo after that; the Sept nowcast row went from -0.94% to -0.80%.

Supercore is graded against BLS services less rent of shelter (CUUR0000SASL2RS) instead of core CPI, which is mostly shelter and core goods. Electricity and utility gas joined medical care, education and communication, recreation and the CPI residual, because BLS counts energy services in that series. The residual's share of supercore falls from 48.5% to 44.6%. It still contains goods, so supercore runs below the BLS series (Aug-2026: 2.71% vs 3.10%). Since 2018 the correlation is 0.930 with a mean absolute gap of 0.70pp. The old grade against core CPI (0.958, 0.56pp) looked better only because it measured the wrong target.

The Heat Check reads seasonally adjusted CPI, core CPI and Case-Shiller (CPIAUCSL, CPILFESL, CSUSHPISA) instead of the unadjusted series. On unadjusted data the 3-month momentum z-scores followed the calendar: the average CPI z ran from -0.89 in December to +1.03 in March (core -0.60 to +1.37, Case-Shiller -0.61 to +1.04). On adjusted data the range is -0.25 to +0.35 (core -0.07 to +0.47, Case-Shiller +0.08 to +0.47).

The DC Hardware storage component no longer rides a level splice of NAND spot prices past the last storage-device PPI. NAND now enters as a like-month year ratio with a pass-through estimated and backtested against realized PPI prints (the treatment the power tail has), and the tail rides only while it beats carry-forward and zero pass-through. NAND collection began 2026-07-15, so no month can be graded until about 2027-08 and storage is official-only until then. Hardware YoY 33.9% (storage tail +117.7%) to 29.3% (storage official Aug +87.2%); the old level tail would have missed the Aug-2026 print by +16.7 YoY points against -1.1 for carry-forward.

The PCE nowcast targets the next PCE (Personal Income & Outlays) release instead of the CPI nowcast's month. Once that month's CPI has printed it bridges from the actual seasonally adjusted CPI, not our CPI forecast; after the month's PPIs print it also uses the four PPIs BEA prices PCE items with (airfares, physicians, hospitals, portfolio management), but only while that bridge beats the CPI-only bridge on the last 24 months out of sample. A core PCE nowcast (bridged from core CPI, benchmarked against the Cleveland Fed) and official core PCE were added. Aug-2026 PCE call: 0.25% (frozen 2026-09-11) to 0.34%; out-of-sample MAE 0.061 vs 0.065pp CPI-only (core 0.060 vs 0.071pp).

The homepage lead-lag statistic is graded on a vintage-true record: the gauge as it could have been known at each month-end (publish-ledger readings since July 2026; before that, each official print applied only from its first release date and each live source only after its publication lag). The old statistic used the hindsight history, which applies every monthly print ~6 weeks before its release. Real-time: 0.951 with CPI one month ahead (same-month corr 0.948, mean gap 0.99pp) vs hindsight 0.945 (0.931, 1.06pp). compare.json publishes the track as `realtime`.

Headline weights vary through history: each date's Σ w·yoy uses BLS relative importance price-updated to that date's own YoY base month (365 days earlier), instead of one month's weights applied to all of 2018-now. Rebuilding official CPI from official component YoYs, June 2022 misses by +0.05pp with its own weights vs -0.26pp with today's; the tracker's correlation with CPI rises 0.9939 -> 0.9978 (mean gap 0.17 -> 0.10pp). Per-month weights are published in replay.json so contribution charts still sum exactly to the headline.

Basket weights are BLS CPI-U relative importance (December tables 2016-2025), price-updated to the YoY base month, replacing the 2026-07-08 seed weights. The seed weights reconstructed Aug-2026 CPI at 3.58% vs the actual 3.40%; the new weights at 3.34%.

"Other" (17.7% of CPI) is the exact CPI residual — CPI-U minus the 13 named components, chained December to December — instead of the 'Other goods and services' index (tobacco and personal care, ~3% of CPI). Aug-2026 YoY 3.21% vs 4.23% for the old proxy.

EIA residential electricity and gas no longer replace published BLS prints; they extend the official series only past the last print, on a like-month ratio. They had substituted July/June EIA data for the published August BLS values, and EIA's residential-gas seasonality inflated the 12-month outlook.

The CPI nowcast is seasonally adjusted (last year's BLS seasonal factors), the basis Cleveland Fed and Kalshi quote; the unadjusted value is kept alongside. Shelter rows follow official OER/rent trend instead of same-month market asking rents. A core-CPI nowcast and a head-to-head leaderboard were added.

Scoreboard actuals are the change as each release reported it (month t over t-1 as known that day), fixing payroll and PCE grades that mixed vintages. Payroll and PCE first prints are backfilled from ALFRED.

DC index proxy tails are anchored on the proxy's reference-month average (PPIs are priced mid-month), not its last value before the month; compute price indexes are chain-linked so members dropping in and out no longer move the level.
Series that are legitimately absent (disclosure-suppressed, intermittent, discontinued) carry an explicit expected-absence policy, judged separately from staleness.

Math audit fixes: the cost-of-living payment index merges MND onto PMMS with level scaling; Heat Check's PPI input sign corrected; the stress index scores consumer credit as growth; nowcast measured rows use month-average moves.
A live source that starts after the blend enters at the blend's level (fixes a fabricated one-day fuel cliff).
Used vehicles ride the Manheim wholesale index with a 30-day lead; Redfin dropped from the shelter blend (dataset retired).
Headline YoY is the weighted mean of each component's own like-month YoY (not an index ratio), so lagging components compare like month to like month.
